briefing: Stocks fell hard today. The NASDAQ dropped 5.3% and the S&P 500 fell 3.7%, so the screener returned no buy candidates. I am making no new buys and keeping all 7 positions, because the automatic -7% stop-losses already protect against bigger losses and selling in a panic at the day's low usually locks in the damage.

daily_lesson.explanation_en: Risk-off is when investors get nervous and sell riskier assets like tech stocks to protect their money, so prices fall quickly across the market. On days like this, a careful investor usually stops buying new stocks and lets stop-loss orders protect the stocks they already own, instead of trying to catch the bottom. Buying is usually safer after the market has settled and is clearly recovering.
daily_lesson.explanation_zh: 「避險情緒」（Risk-Off）是指投資者轉趨審慎，紛紛拋售科技股等高風險資產以保本，令大市急速下跌。遇上這種日子，審慎的投資者一般會暫停建立新倉，並以止蝕盤保障現有持倉，而非急於撈底。待市況回穩、出現明確反彈訊號後再入市，通常較為穩妥。

market_education.summary_en: Broad selling hit US stocks today, and the NASDAQ (-5.3%) fell harder than the S&P 500 (-3.7%). That pattern usually means investors are pulling money out of growth and tech stocks, which carry higher valuations, and moving it somewhere safer. No news headlines came with today's data, so the exact trigger can't be named here, but a one-day drop this large is a clear risk-off signal.
market_education.summary_zh: 美股今日全面受壓，納指重挫5.3%，跌幅明顯大於標普500指數的3.7%。這種走勢通常反映資金正撤出估值較高的科技及成長股，轉往較安全的資產避險。今日數據未附相關新聞標題，因此未能指出確切的觸發因素，但單日跌幅如此之大，已是明確的避險訊號。
